title: Ageing and Treatments
body: Fill an ageing vessel with compatible wine to begin its work, then collect the finished wine with an empty hand when it is ready. Ordinary barrels take four bottles; a cellar cask treatment provides an eight-bottle vessel.

The wood family changes an ordinary barrel's appearance, not its functional treatment. To specialize an empty ordinary Aging Barrel, hold a Cooper's Mallet and a treatment kit, then use either on the barrel. Toasting, seasoning and cask conversion provide different ageing choices while keeping its wood appearance.

Toasted barrels mature wine faster and favour a bolder red-wine profile. Seasoned barrels work more gently and slowly, while cellar casks offer slower bulk maturation. These are trade-offs rather than a ladder in which one choice always produces the best bottle.

Use the Almanac on the vessel for its live reading. Sneak-use it for the additional treatment guide and crafting hint. The vessel's contribution, the wine it holds and the surrounding cellar all matter; a decorative wood change is not a quality upgrade.
